content:
A palindrome with an even number of digits has each digit occurring twice, so its digit sum would be even. Since the required digit sum is \(13\), which is odd, the palindrome must have an odd number of digits.

Let the palindrome have length \(2k+1\), with central digit \(c\) and \(k\) pairs of outer digits. Then the digit sum is

\[
2(\text{sum of outer digits}) + c = 13.
\]

So \(c\) must be odd, and

\[
\text{sum of outer digits} = \frac{13-c}{2}.
\]

For each odd central digit \(c\), count the number of sequences of positive digits whose sum is \(\frac{13-c}{2}\), for any possible number of outer pairs \(k\). The number of compositions of a positive integer \(S\) into any number of positive parts is \(2^{S-1}\).

Now compute for each possible odd \(c\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
c & S=\frac{13-c}{2} & \text{number of choices} \\
\hline
1 & 6 & 2^{5}=32 \\
3 & 5 & 2^{4}=16 \\
5 & 4 & 2^{3}=8 \\
7 & 3 & 2^{2}=4 \\
9 & 2 & 2^{1}=2
\end{array}
\]

Adding these gives

\[
32+16+8+4+2=62.
\]

\[
\boxed{62}
\]
